analysis:
The only changed lines in provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/ProviderLoop+ModelLoading.swift are around head lines 1189-1191, in the unload path. A non-shutdown unload now skips persistLoadedModelSet() when servingDrain.owner == .addonHold. The persisted set is the startup-preload plan, so an add-on hold's temporary unload no longer drops the model from it. This mirrors the existing shutdown behavior.

Security impact appears limited to availability and persistence semantics. It touches no crypto, attestation, authorization, coordinator-wire, or prefix-cache behavior. The T-041 cache controls are unaffected: SSD cache eligibility is still driven by the fresh bracketing weight-hash checks in ensureModelLoaded, which are unchanged (base lines 549-662). Skipping the persist keeps the model's identity in a local startup list only. The next boot's preload still goes through ensureModelLoaded with its weight-hash, admission, and runtime-eligibility gates.

Unverified integration points are outside the supplied units. These are the definition of servingDrain.owner/.addonHold, whether the hold is always released or cleared (otherwise the persisted set could go stale), and whether the set is validated at preload. These are low-risk questions and do not support a finding.

I also examined the unchanged load path in the supplied base text: hash bracketing, the pending-load lease, and the unwind ordering. I found no new regression from this PR.
